span.p:
Process-create event observed
(parent process -> child process)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Is this parent->child pair on the
environment's documented, expected-lineage baseline?
(e.g. explorer.exe -> outlook.exe)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
EXPECTED
No alert. Log for baseline only.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Has this exact pair been observed
before in this environment,
just infrequently?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
RARE
Surface to hunt queue.
No standing alert on its own.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Does the child's command line carry
an aggravating signal -
encoded/obfuscated arguments,
a remote-content fetch, or a
credential-store target path?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
SUSPICIOUS
Tier-1 alert. Triage against
known-admin-tool allowlist first.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
HIGHLY SUSPICIOUS
Tier-2 alert. Treat as likely
post-exploitation until disproven.
